metadata.title: Influencer Regulation RAG Chatbot Evaluation Dataset
metadata.corpus: European Commission Influencer Legal Hub, Legal Briefs #1-#10
metadata.purpose: Evaluate retrieval, answer correctness, quotation/evidence grounding, and decision support.
metadata.important_note: Gold quotations are deliberately short evidence anchors. The evaluator should verify exact quotation presence against the chatbot's corpus before scoring.

questions.question: Why does EU consumer law matter to influencers who regularly advertise or sell products?

gold_answer.summary: Regular commercial activity can make an influencer a trader subject to consumer-protection obligations.
key_points: regular commercial activity can trigger trader status

gold_quotations.quote: When you do business on a regular basis, European law will see you as a ‘trader’.

questions.question: Does EU consumer protection apply only to large companies?

gold_answer.summary: No. The materials explain that trader obligations can apply to one-person businesses as well as large companies.
key_points: consumer obligations are not limited to large companies

questions.question: Is the Influencer Legal Hub presented as an exhaustive statement of every law that can apply to influencers?

gold_answer.summary: No. The Hub presents selected important EU rules and explains that other national, media and self-regulatory rules can also matter.
key_points: the materials are a selection, not an exhaustive code
gold_answer.legal_caution: Do not treat the Hub as a complete substitute for jurisdiction-specific legal advice.
